Elect Mike van Gorder for City Council to keep Burbank on the right track for progress. Mike Van Gorder is a state housing policy expert, tenants’ rights activist, and community organizer. He is a senior housing policy specialist for the State of California, a Burbank planning commissioner, and founder of the Glendale Tenants Union. Van Gorder’s priorities include combating the housing crisis, boosting worker power, protecting public education, and standing up for all Burbankers. He is endorsed by California Working Families Party, LA DSA, Burbank Teachers Association, East Area Progressive Democrats, Housing Action Coalition, UNITE HERE Local 11, Asm. Alex Lee, Burbank City Councilmember Konstantine Anthony, Burbank Planning Commissioner Jason Bennett, and Burbank School Board Member Dr. Armond Aghakhanian. Elect Nolan Southerland for City Council to keep Burbank on the right track for progress. Nolan Southerland is a community organizer and a 15-year union member of IATSE Local 700. He is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America and works with the Burbank Tenants Union. Southerland’s priorities include affordable housing, welcoming immigrants, transportation, better jobs, supporting youth, a greener Burbank, and public safety. He is endorsed by DSA-LA, Los Angeles County Federation of Labor, UNITE HERE Local 11, California Working Families Party, Streets for All, Los Angeles League of Conservation Voters, California Democratic Renters Council, LA City Controller Kenneth Mejia, and Burbank City Councilmember Konstantine Anthony. Elect Helen Krieger for City Council to keep West Hollywood on the right track for progress. Helen Krieger is a TV writer and former neighborhood association president. As president, she helped convert a historic factory into 37 units of affordable apartments for working artists and musicians. Krieger’s priorities include affordable housing, safe streets, thriving local business, bringing filming back to WeHo, LGBTQIA+ rights, environmental sustainability, and a transparent, fiscally responsible government. She is endorsed by Los Angeles County Democratic Party, Los Angeles County Federation of Labor, Equality California, Westside Young Democrats, California Working Families Party, Moms Demand Action, LA Supervisor Lindsay Horvath, West Hollywood City Councilmember John Erickson, and Culver City Council Member and Vice Mayor Bryan ‘Bubba’ Fish. References: https://www.helen4weho.org/ Read More

Elect Stephen Post for City Council to keep West Hollywood on the right track for progress. Stephen Post is a nonprofit advocate, community organizer, and a business program manager at the Los Angeles Neighborhood Initiative. He has worked at the Last Prisoner Project, served on the West Hollywood Public Safety Commission and the Columbus Area Planning Commission, and was part of the WeHo 2040 Strategic Plan team. Post was also president of CGS at Ohio State, and formed the Pregnant and Parenting Students Support Committee while there. His top priorities include strengthening rent stabilization, building public housing, participatory budgeting, protecting trans and LGBTQIA+ rights, publicly funded elections, proactive homelessness prevention, safe and clean streets, and fighting ICE and federal attacks. Post is endorsed by California Working Families Party, LA DSA, Los Angeles County Young Democrats, UNITE HERE Local 1, Sunrise Movement LA, LA City Controller Kenneth Mejia, LA City Councilmember Eunisses Hernandez, Rent Stabilization Commissioner Rena Goldman, and Public Safety Commissioner Catherine Eng. Last updated: 9/26/2026 References: https://www.post4weho.com/ Read More

subject.title: Anaheim Elementary School District Board, Trustee Area 2

positions.statement: Re-elect Juan Gabriel Álvarez as Trustee to keep Anaheim Elementary School District Board on the right track for progress. Álvarez has served as Trustee for Area 2 since 2018, when he won 52% of the vote. He is a bilingual junior high math teacher and a founding member of SOMOS Anaheim and founder of Operation L.E.E. (Literacy Engaging Everyone). Álvarez recently served on the City of Anaheim’s Cultural and Heritage Commission. He is endorsed by Chispa and California Working Families Party. Álvarez earned his bachelor’s degree from California State University, Fullerton and his master’s from California State University-Long Beach. Álvarez was the first person in his family to attend college. The Race General election: Two candidates are running in the nonpartisan November 3 general election: Juan Gabriel Álvarez (incumbent) and Jeff Cole. The Position Anaheim Elementary School District serves 17,000 students at 24 schools and employs more than 2,000 people. The Board of Education has five trustees. subject.title: Anaheim Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 1

positions.statement: Re-elect Trustee Jessica Guerrero to keep Anaheim Union High School District Board on the right track for progress. Jessica Guerrero has served as trustee for Area 1 since she was elected in 2022 with 44% of the vote in a field of three candidates, and is currently the board president. She was the first Latina elected to the seat, in a district where more than 70% of students are Latino. As a trustee, Guerrero has strengthened collaboration with the community to address food insecurity, expand student internships, and support student safety. She is a policy advisor for the Orange County Board of Supervisors and leads an internship program. Guerrero previously served as a teaching assistant at UC-Irvine. She and her family are graduates of Anaheim public schools. Guerrero earned her bachelor’s in public administration from California State University-Fullerton, and master’s in public policy from the University of California-Irvine, and was a first-generation college student. She is endorsed by Orange County Young Democrats, OC Action, Chispa, State Superintendent of Public Instruction Tony Thurmond, Orange County Supervisor Vicente Sarmiento, Anaheim Mayor Ashleigh Aitken, and many education leaders. The Position The Anaheim Union High School Board of Trustees has five members. Trustees serve four-year terms. Last updated: 9/26/26 References: https://www.auhsd.us/District/Department/14174-Board/80153-Board-of-Trustees.html https://www.voteguerrero.com/ Read More

Garcia is a Big with Big Brothers Big Sisters of Orange County and the Inland Empire, and a math and science tutor to middle and high school students. He earned his bachelor’s in mechanical engineering from Iowa State University. Garcia is endorsed by Chispa and California Working Families Party. Jozef Maldonado is a chemist, a community leader, and a member of the Fullerton Parks and Recreation Commission. He has worked to elect leaders and has organized alongside labor unions, neighborhood advocates, and community organizations. Maldonado's top issues are public safety, services for seniors, small-business development, and supporting working families. He built the Equity in OC Initiative to increase access to resources across Orange County, and previously co-founded an organization focused on the needs of LGBTQIA+ Vietnamese community. Nguyen’s top issues are strengthening city services, expanding outdoor and public areas, improving mental health services, and addressing the high cost of housing. He has the endorsement of Working Families Party, OC Action, the Democratic Party of Orange County, Chispa, Women for American Values and Ethics, Orange County Labor Federation, and Planned Parenthood. Elect Jose Rodriguez for Mayor to keep National City on the right track for progress. Jose Rodriguez has served as National City Council member since 2020. In his tenure, he worked on a short-term rentals ordinance, homeownership development, a legal defense fund for residents facing deportation, human trafficking prevention and enforcement, a district-level streetlight survey, and Adopt-a-Tree campaigns. Rodriguez’s priorities are affordable housing, community safety, economic growth, and environmental health. Prior to the city council, he worked at a regional labor union, a tenants’ rights group, and on the campaign of San Diego Rep. Juan Vargas. subject.title: San Diego Unified School District Board, District C

positions.statement: Elect Hayden Gore as Board Trustee to keep San Diego Unified School District on the right track for progress. Gore is a longtime bilingual educator who currently teaches at High Tech Middle Chula Vista. He co-founded the High Tech Education Collective to represent the more than 700 educators and support staff across High Tech High, served as its first president for four years, and led the union to its first contract. Gore previously taught as part of the Peace Corps and in rural schools in Guatemala, and directed the International Training Program for the Peruvian Forensic Anthropology Team. His top priorities are ensuring that schools are safe, inclusive, and nurturing spaces for all students, families, and staff; investing district resources in classrooms and student supports; and supporting efforts to develop affordable housing for educators, staff, and families on district land. Gore is endorsed by the San Diego Education Association, the San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council, the American Federation of Teachers Local 1931, San Diego Democrats for Equality, Asm. Chris Ward, and four trustees of the San Diego Unified School District. The RaceGeneral election: Hayden Gore is running unopposed in the November 3 general election. The PositionThe San Diego Unified School District Board of Education has five trustees and two student board members. Board trustees serve four-year terms, and have a three-term limit. Read More

Elect Naindeep Singh for City Council to keep Fresno on the right track for progress. Naindeep Singh is a Central Unified board trustee and executive director of Jakara Movement, a grassroots community-building organization for Punjabi Sikhs and other marginalized communities. His top issues include fighting for an affordable Fresno, investing in an infrastructure future, putting small businesses first, building affordability and housing, supporting schools, youth, LGBTQIA+, and immigrants, and restoring trust in Fresno. Singh has the endorsement of Asm. Esmeralda Soria, Fresno Unified Trustees Andy Levine and Susan Wittrup, CAIR Action, ValleyVotersPAC, UFCW 8, and the California Working Families Party. The Race June 2 primary results: Naindeep Singh 39%, Robert Fuentes 37%, Joe Hinojosa 13%, and Monte Forkas 12%. Naindeep Singh and Robert Fuentes will contend in the November 3 general election. This is a nonpartisan race. The Position Fresno is governed by a seven-person city council. A city council is responsible for establishing policy, passing local laws (called ordinances), voting on budget appropriations, and developing an overall vision for the city with the mayor. subject.title: Fresno Unified School District Board, Area 4

positions.statement: Re-elect Veva Islas as Trustee to keep Fresno Unified School District on the right track for progress. Islas has served on the Fresno Unified School District Board of Education since 2019, when she was elected with 45% of the vote in a three-candidate field, and is the current president. In her time on the board, she has championed parent engagement and language justice, expanded dual-enrollment opportunities, grown Career Technical Education programs, and expanded bilingual and biliteracy programs. Islas is also dedicated to early childhood education, improved school facilities, fiscal responsibility, and work-based learning opportunities. She is founder and executive director of Cultiva La Salud, a public health advocacy nonprofit in Fresno. She is endorsed by California Working Families Party, Fresno County Democratic Women’s Club, Planned Parenthood Advocates Mar Monte, Progressive PAC, National Women’s Political Caucus Fresno, Asm. Joaquin Arambula, and Fresno Unified School District Trustee Andy Levine. The RaceGeneral election: Three candidates are running in the nonpartisan November 3 general election: Veva Islas (incumbent), Mirna Garcia, and Karen Steed. The PositionFresno Unified School District Board of Education serves 70,000 students and 10,000 staff 2,000 people. The Board of Education has six trustees. Read More

Re-elect Councilmember Eric Arias to keep Bakersfield on the right track for progress. Arias has served on Bakersfield City Council since 2020, when he was elected with 74% of the vote, and is president and CEO of United Way of Central Eastern California. As councilmember, he has fought for fairer district maps, Southeast Bakersfield investments, park improvements, traffic calming, affordable housing, and balanced budgets that protect core city services. Arias’s top priorities include reducing crime and strengthening public safety, improving quality of life, and fighting for Ward 1’s fair share of investment. He volunteers for Leaders in LIfe and We the People. Arias is endorsed by the Kern County Democratic Central Committee; the Kern, Inyo and Mono Counties Central Labor Council; SEIU Local 521; Planned Parenthood; Asm. Esmeralda Soria; Kern County Supervisor Leticia Perez; Bakersfield City Council Member Manpreet Kaur; and California State Regional Director Noe Garcia. The RaceGeneral election: Two candidates are running in the nonpartisan November 3 general election: Eric Arias (incumbent) and Mercy Peña. The PositionBakersfield is governed by a seven-person city council. A city council is responsible for establishing policy, passing local laws (called ordinances), voting on budget appropriations, and developing an overall vision for the city. Councilmembers serve four-year terms. Read More

positions.statement: Elect Celest Mendoza to City Council to put Santa Maria on the right track for progress. Celest Mendoza is a program manager at Goodwill Industries, where she supports youth, adults, and families across Santa Barbara County and leads community outreach. She serves on the board of the Lompoc Teen Center. Mendoza’s priorities are affordability, opportunity, and accountability. She is endorsed by CAUSE Action Fund, Santa Barbara County Democratic Party, Santa Barbara Young Democrats, Indivisible Santa Maria, Planned Parenthood Central Coast Action Fund, and United Domestic Workers. Re-elect Councilmember Gloria Soto to keep Santa Maria on the right track for progress. Gloria Soto has served on the Santa Maria City Council since 2018, when she was the youngest woman elected to the council. She is the executive director of Future Leaders of America, one of California’s largest Latinx youth-serving organizations, and a board member of the Fund for Santa Barbara, the Allan Hancock Foundation, 805 UndocuFund, and One Community Action. Soto previously worked at Planned Parenthood California Central Coast. Her priorities are affordable housing, youth and families, and small-business vitality. positions.statement: Elect Alex Vara for Superintendent to keep San Bernardino County on the right track for progress. Alex Vara has 34 years of experience in education as a former middle school principal, teacher, and aide in Rialto Unified School District. He served on the Redlands Unified School District board, California Interscholastic Federation board, and Colton-Redlands-Yucaipa Regional Occupational Program board. Vara trained future teachers at California State University-San Bernardino. His top priorities are safe classrooms for all, resources to support every child, and career and college pathways starting in middle school. Vara has the endorsement of the Redlands Teachers Association, Redlands Education Support Professionals Association, and California Working Families Party. The RaceJune 2 primary election results: Cali Binks 39%, Alex Vara 31%, Ray Anthony Culberson 15%, and Ken Larson 15%. Cali Binks and Alex Vara will contend in the November 3 general election. This is a nonpartisan race. The PositionThe San Bernardino County superintendent of schools oversees the San Bernardino County Office of Education, which provides instruction and services for nearly 400,000 K–12 public school students.
